title: Friction-reduction release canvas + 3-week rollout calendar
body:
Purpose:
Reduce rollout friction for the upcoming runtime+routing change by codifying small, repeatable checks, a tight 3-week cadence, and a short draft of release notes. This doc is a working canvas for launch engineers and product owners — aim: predictable, low-latency rollouts with clear gates.

Executive summary (one line):
Iterative canary over 3 weeks with automated telemetry gates, scoped feature flags, and a lightweight rollback playbook. Primary risk: small regression in multi-tenant KV cache performance under long-seq workloads.

3-week rollout calendar (compact) — owners in parentheses:
- Week A (Oct 12–18): integration smoke + safety lab (owner: Priya)
  - Deploy to staging and dedicated QA pools on Mon (low-traffic day)
  - Run long-seq replay (10k tokens baseline) against canary images
  - Validate cost-per-token telemetry baseline and KV cache hit-rate 
- Week B (Oct 19–25): micro-canary (owner: Miles)
  - Mon: Canary1 -> 1% production traffic ; Tue: stable-checks ; Thu: 5% ; Fri: 10%
  - Daily check-in (15m) 09:30 PT in #release-orchestra
- Week C (Oct 26–Nov 1): ramp + broaden (owner: Anika)
  - Mon: 25% traffic if gates pass; Wed: 50%
  - Fri: 100% if all telemetry and latency SLOs hold; otherwise hold and investigate

Preflight (48–72h) micro-checklist (owner next to item):
- Confirm canary image tag and SHA (Miles)
- Verify model catalog pinning and fallback variants are configured (Anika)
- Confirm autoscaler limits and burst policy set for Dedicated pools (Infra lead)
- KMS key rotation planned during non-critical window (Security)
- Observability: smoke dashboards ready, alert routing to paging channel (SRE)
- Canary traffic policy defined in routing service and validated in dry-run (Eng-release)
- Licence/contract check for third-party model runtime (Legal/PM)

Launch-time quick checks (day-of):
- Sanity endpoints: /health, /model/ping, /cache/stats — responses within baseline (<= 2x normal)
- Token generation latency 50th/95th/99th percentile check (compare to previous 7-day baseline)
- Error rate spike threshold: >0.75% needs immediate pause and review
- Cost per 1k tokens drift: >12% increase -> flag (billing)

Canary shepherding policy (conservative defaults):
- Step sizes: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%
- Minimum hold window per step: 24 hours (unless major regressions observed)
- Telemetry gates (all must be green to advance):
  - Latency: 95p must stay within +15% of baseline
  - Errors: request error rate < 0.75% and trending down
  - KV cache hit-rate: no >5% absolute drop versus baseline
  - Cost: cost-per-token +-12%
  - Quality: run 200 synthetic prompts (open-qa + chat scenarios); F1/ROUGE/semantic-sim thresholds defined in linked eval
- Automatic rollback triggers: any single gate violation marked as critical by oncall -> immediate rollback to previous platform image and notify owners

Observability smoke checklist (SRE):
- Dashboards: release-orchestra/latency, release-orchestra/errors, release-orchestra/costs, release-orchestra/kvcache
- Alerting: page-on (severity P1) for error spikes or latency SLO breaches; page-on (P2) for cost anomalies
- Logging: correlate request-id across edge, router, and runtime logs; ensure 100% request-id propagation for 7 sampled requests
- Tracing: end-to-end traces exist for 99% of sampled requests during canary window

Rollback criteria and fast paths:
- Immediate rollback: sustained error rate >1% for 30m OR 95p latency >25% for 30m
- Fast rollback command: infra/roll-back --to-image sha:XXXX --region all
- Soft rollback (partial): re-route 80% of canary traffic to fallback model-variant; leave 20% for forensics
- Communications: notify #release-orchestra, send status to release-cadence@redwood.com, update incident doc template

Post-deploy checklist (first 72h):
- Confirm full traffic at 100% is stable for 48h (no gate breaches)
- Snapshot telemetry and attach to PR and Confluence notes (owner: Miles)
- Run regression eval set and compare to pre-release baseline; file tickets for any drift > threshold (owner: Priya)
- Schedule 1-week retro and 30-day stability digest (Anika)

Draft release notes (for product/marketing review) — short bullets:
- Feature: routing policy layered fallback — route requests automatically to verified model-variants when capacity is constrained; reduces tail failures for mixed-tenant workloads.
- Runtime: KV-cache improvements — reduced cache warm-up on long sequences, targeted to improve latency for streaming chat sessions.
- Ops: New canary shepherding and auto-rollback gates; release engineers can now perform progressive ramps with automated telemetry checks.
- Migration notes: No client changes required. Operators pinned fallback configs may be updated via Console. Customers on private deployments should coordinate with Solutions to schedule node restarts.
- Known issues: Under specific long-sequence workloads (>8k tokens) we have observed a 3–6% QoL regression on a small internal eval set — mitigations: fallback to quantized variant (see linked PR).

Unresolved questions / TODOs (short):
- Who will be runbook owner during the weekend window (Oct 24–25)? -> need primary/secondary
- Confirm dedicated pool CPU/mem headroom numbers with Platform (action: Liam)
- Add a short synthetic suite that exercises token-by-token streaming behaviors (Priya)
- Validate billing alert thresholds with Finance before full ramp

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Keep the micro-canary window to specific low-traffic hours if possible; avoid overlapping with major customer batches (check calendar)
- If we see KV-cache hit-rate drop, do not immediately increase traffic; step back and run targeted replay
- Keep release notes tight; capture technical details in Confluence link above for CS and Solutions

Appendix (useful links and snippets):
- Canary rollback command snippet: "infractl rollback --image sha:abc123 --regions us-west1,us-east1"
- Quick verification curl: curl -sS -H 'x-release-check: true' https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq '.'
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/release/2026-q4

End of canvas — use this as the single source during launch planning. Iterate and move sections into the formal runbook when stabilized.

---
Draft meta: lightweight, intentionally informal. Will convert to formal runbook after green 100% for 72h.
